key_insight: Cu feedstock morphology governs impact deformation in cold-sprayed Cu–Al₂O₃ composites: spherical particles localize strain at splat interfaces, while spongy particles distribute strain through ligament collapse.
engineering_relevance: Feedstock morphology offers a design lever alongside spray parameters for tailoring composite coating microstructure and mechanical performance.
method: Compare deposits produced from spherical and spongy Cu feedstocks.
Evaluate micro-compression behavior and tribological performance.
evidence_signal: Multi-scale characterization links spherical Cu to refined splat boundaries and coarser cores, and spongy Cu to distributed strain hardening and greater ceramic encapsulation, with performance differences even at comparable reinforcement fractions.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance gains or processing window, limiting direct translation into production specifications.
paper_title: Feedstock Morphology Governs Impact-Induced Deformation in Cold Sprayed Metal-Ceramic Composites
